speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic; I see you have swelling in your right knee and a family history of similar issues. To begin, can you tell me exactly when this swelling started and if you have experienced any trauma or sudden injury?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (Oligoarticular) or Early-Onset Septic Arthritis. Given the patient's age (18 months), sudden onset without trauma, unilateral swelling, and a family history suggesting a genetic predisposition (e.g., HLA-B27 association or familial osteoarthropathy), the differential is broad. I need to distinguish between inflammatory, infectious, and crystal-induced causes. Let's proceed with targeted imaging and labs.

REQUEST TEST: ESR, CRP, CBC, and RF/ANA.
REQUEST IMAGES: Right Knee X-ray (AP and Lateral views) and right knee Ultrasound.

*Note: While the patient is 18 months old, the description of an "uncle with similar problems" raises questions about a genetic condition. However, without more specific family details, I will focus on the acute presentation first.*
